newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Holocaust fund to pay any suit damages - UBS.
newsitem.headline: Holocaust fund to pay any suit damages - UBS.

text.p: UBS said any claims Swiss banks might be forced to pay as a result of three huge class-action suits by Holocaust victims over banks' World War Two role must be paid from a newly created Swiss Holocaust memorial fund.

UBS Chairman Robert Studer said the bank had not made any provisions for paying potential damages that might arise from the suits for billions of dollars filed in U.S. courts and alleging that banks hoarded Holocaust victims' wealth.
"Any potential claims will have to be settled from this (fund)," Studer told UBS's annual shareholders' meeting.
"We have not made any provisions for any damages related to the class-action suits," he added.

UBS and the two other biggest Swiss banks together donated 100 million Swiss francs for the humanitarian fund for Holocaust survivors. Smaller banks, the Swiss National Bank and private companies have pledged another 165 million.
UBS spokeswoman Gerturd Erismann said it made sense to settle any future damages from the fund because the class-action suits were aimed against Swiss banks in general.
She said the suits named UBS and its two biggest rivals -- Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Bank Corp -- but also included the National Bank and unnamed other Swiss banks.

Erismann said UBS was in negotiations with the plaintiffs in the U.S., but added these talks had so far been limited to points of legal procedure about how the cases should be tried and whether the banks would have to disclose all their records.
Erismann said there had been no talks as yet with the U.S. plaintiffs about the substance of the suits or the possibility of out-of-court settlements.
